Print a filter result

Source: R/plots.R
print.mhp.Rd

print() of a result of hp_filter(), mhp_filter() or fmhp_filter() (with as_dt = FALSE) shows the smoothing parameter, the criterion and summaries of the cycle, as in version 0.1.0, and the sources of the method.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mhp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a result of hp_filter(), mhp_filter() or fmhp_filter() with as_dt = FALSE.

...

further arguments (digits).

Value

x, invisibly.

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(us_macro)
m <-
  mhp_filter(
      x          = log(us_macro$gdp)
    , max_lambda = 100000
    , as_dt      = FALSE
    , log_scale  = FALSE
    , criterion  = c("approximate", "exact")
    )
print(x = m)
#> Modified HP Filter Result
#> ==============================
#> Observations: 203 
#> Optimal lambda: 683 
#> GCV: 2.82e-04 
#> 
#> Cycle Statistics:
#>   Mean: -1.634e-13 
#>   SD:   0.01333 
#>   AR1:  0.828 
#>   Range: 0.07802 
#> 
#> Sources: Hodrick and Prescott (1997); McDermott (1997); Coe and McDermott
#> (1997); Choudhary et al. (2014); Choudhary et al. (2014, MATLAB code). Full
#> references: mhp_cite(x).
